facts.text: The appellant challenged the correctness of that order by filing a petition under Art. 226 of the Constitution in the High Court of Bombay at Nagpur, but that petition was dismissed as the award was made before its hearing.

facts.text: On June 3, 1957, the Industrial Court made an award holding that the Corporation was an industry and all departments of the Corporation were covered by the said definition and revised the pay scales.

facts.text: A division bench of the High Court by its order dated September 11, 1957 rejected the contention that the Corporation was not an industry and remanded the case to the State Industrial Court.

facts.text: On remand, the Industrial Court held that all departments of the Corporation except those dealing with assessment and levy of house-tax, assessment and levy of octroi, removal of encroachment and removal and pulling down of dilapidated houses, prevention and control of food adulteration, and maintenance of cattle pounds were covered by the definition of industry.
